mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and CPI inflation above 4% for two consecutive months signals a stagflationary environment, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% AND CPIAUCSL > 104 (i.e., >4% YoY) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the civilian unemployment rate by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by > -0.5% in one month (i.e., rises by >0.5pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates reduced household investment and consumption intent, which negatively impacts GDP growth and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real GDP growth (GDPC1 QoQ change) and S&P 500 20-day forward returns; higher GDP growth signals improved corporate earnings and investor optimism, leading to positive returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between GDPC1 QoQ growth and S&P 500 20-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) over any 5-year rolling window.
